Criminal Procedure Code, the petitioners have prayed for their enlargement on bail, in FIR No.32 of 2020, dated 27.12.2020, registered under Sections 376D, 323 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter to be referred as 'IPC') Act, at Police Station Kullu, District Kullu, H.P.
2.

Brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present petitions are that on 27.12.2020, SHO,
Women Police Station, Kullu, District Kullu, H.P. on the basis of rapat No.8, dated 27.12.2020,
reached Regional Hospital, Kullu, where she met one Kavita Pillai, who informed her that the victim was her sister who did not appear to be in a fit mental condition as she was shouting continuously and loudly that she had been molested.
In terms of the Medico Legal Certificate, the Doctor opined that the patient was not showing suitable psychotic behaviour and her mental condition was not stable.

The FIR was lodged at the behest of Kavita Pillai and in the course of investigation, the present petitioners alongwith one Niraj Singh were arrested on the alleged ground of having outrage the modesty of the accused.

The petitioners are in custody since 27.12.2022.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners have argued that both the petitioners are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the case.

They submitted that the investigation which has been .
carried out in the matter as well as statements of the prosecution witnesses which sand recorded till date, nowhere point out towards culpability of the petitioners visavis the offence alleges to have been committed by them.
They further argued that even the report of the Forensic Science Laboratory does not supports the case of the prosecution.

They further argued that the petitioners are young boys, who are in custody for more than two and half years now and taking into consideration the fact that progress in the case stands stalled since the month of August, 2022, on Aman Jaiswal vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13093803/

, it will be in the interest of justice in case present petitions are allowed and the petitioners are ordered to be released on bail.
They submit that in the event of the petitioners being released on bail, they will be abide by all the conditions imposed upon them.

4. The prayer is opposed by learned Additional Advocate General, who has argued that taking into consideration the gravity and heinousness of the offence alleged to have been committed by the petitioners, it would not be in the interest of justice if the petitioners are released on bail, because there is each and every possibility that they will try to intimidate the prosecution witnesses as well as remaining witnesses whose statements are remained to be recorded, which will cause prejudice to the fair trial of the case.

He .
further argued that taking into consideration the stage at which the trial presently is, interest of justice demands that present petitions be dismissed as the petitioners who are guilty of having committed heinous offence, do not deserve the discretion of the Court.
Accordingly, he submitted that present petitions be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the status reports filed from time to time.
I have also carefully gone perused the documents which stand appended with the petitions.
6. The factual matrix which led to the arrest of the petitioners has already been dwelled by me hereinabove.
Whether or not, the petitioners are guilty of the offence alleged to have been committed by them, is of course is a matter of trial.

There is no doubt that the allegation against the petitioners indeed is grave, but this Court can also not lose sight of the fact that the petitioners are in custody for more than two and half years now since 27.12.2020.

7. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Kartar Singh Versus State of Punjab, (1994) 3 Supreme Court Cases 569 and thereafter, in Shaheen Welfare Association Versus Union of India and others, (1996)
2 Supreme Court Cases 616, has taken note of it recently by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohd.
Muslim Islam @ Hussain Versus State (NCT of Delhi), Criminal Appeal No(s). of 2023 [@ Special .
Leave Petition (CRL.) No.(s).915 of 2023], decided on 28.03.2023, has been pleased to observe and reiterate that when stringent provisions are enacted, curtailing the provisions of bail, and restricting of bail, and restricting judicial discretion, it is on the basis that investigation and trials would be concluded swiftly.

fact of the matter remains that whether or not, an accused alleged to have been committed an Aman Jaiswal vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13093803/

sentences.text: The contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that progress in the trial is hanging fire since the month of August, 2022, on account of nonappearance of the prosecutrix for having her cross examination recorded before the learned Special Judge, could not be disputed by the learned Additional Advocate General during the course of arguments of the present petitions.

In fact, the Court has been apprised that as from 23.08.2022, the prosecutrix was summoned for 15.09.2022,
28.09.2022, 11.11.2022, 09.12.2022, 20.02.2023, 21.02.2023, 18.05.2023 and 19.05.2023, .
for recording of her crossexamination, but she did not appear before the Court.

10. This being the fact situation, this Court is of the considered view that as there is no guaranty that the prosecutrix would make herself available for her crossexamination in the near future also, the interest of justice demands that the present petitioners be ordered to be released on bail.

In fact, the bail petition by petitioner Aman Jaiswal was filed in the month of March, 2023 itself, but adjudication thereof was deferred by this Court on the request of the State, so that on the subsequent dates of hearing so given by the learned Special Judge, the State could get the cross examination of the prosecutrix recorded in the interest of justice.

However, as nothing has been transpired since filing of the petitions till date, especially on account of nonappearance of the prosecutrix for having her crossexamination recorded, no purpose is going to be served by further detaining the present petitioners in jail and it would be in the interest of justice to enlarge them on bail.

As far as the apprehension expressed by the learned Additional Advocate General with the regard to the petitioners try to create any hindrance in smooth holding of the trial is concerned, liberty is being granted to the State that in case the petitioners overreach any of the conditions imposed upon them or create any impediment in .
the course of the fair trial, they shall be at liberty to move appropriate application for cancellation of the bail.

The petitions stand disposed of in the above terms.

11. Accordingly, these petitions are allowed, by ordering the petitioners release on bail in FIR No.32 of 2020, dated 27.12.2020, registered under Sections 376D, 323 and 506 of the IPC, at Police Station Kullu, District Kullu, H.P., on their furnishing personal bail bond to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/ each, with one surety in the like amount each, to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court concerned, within a period of two weeks from today, subject to the following conditions:  i.)
Petitioners shall attend the trial Court on each and every date of hearing and if prevented by any reason to do so, seek exemption from appearance by filing appropriate application;  ii.) They shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence nor hamper the investigation of the case in any manner whatsoever;
iii) They shall not make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her/them from disclosing such facts to the Court or the Police Officer; and
